title: Controlplane Deployability and Objection Frames
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, operational GTM brief for field sellers and solutions engineers that blends message framing (control plane deployability), quick rebuttals to regulated-workload objections, and a lightweight technical appendix for engineering conversations. This is intentionally pragmatic: short soundbites + a prioritized list of buyer concerns + demo checklist for low-friction validation calls.

Audience:
- Account executives and AE engineering partners
- Solutions engineers and sales engineers supporting regulated buyers
- Product marketing preparing pitch decks and battlecards

Status / context notes:
- Draft for review by Product, Security, and SE leads.
- Pulls together customer-facing learnings from three pilot engagements in Q3 and SRE runbooks from Dedicated/Private onprem pilots.
- Open questions at bottom for legal and infra to confirm.

TL;DR Positioning (one-liners to use early)
- "Redwood lets you run inference behind your network boundary while we keep control-plane complexity out of your day-to-day: we orchestrate, you retain traffic and keys."
- "For regulated workloads we offer a minimal, auditable control-plane snapshot that integrates with your KMS and SIEM — no data plane egress unless you explicitly enable it."
- "You get predictable performance and the same API contract as hosted mode, so app engineers don’t rewrite clients during migration."

Top buyer personas and their primary concerns
- CISO / Security Architect: isolation, data egress controls, auditability of control plane changes, key management.
- Head of Compliance / Privacy Officer: certification expectations (SOC2, ISO, FedRAMP), data residency, ability to provide evidence to auditors.
- Platform/Infra Lead: deployment ergonomics, upgrade policies, rollback procedures, integration with existing tooling (Terraform, ArgoCD), operational cost.
- ML/Feature Owner: model versioning, latency guarantees, reproducible rollout and rollback, ability to route to fallback models.

Prioritized buyer objections + one-line rebuttals and supporting detail
1) "We can’t trust an external control plane — it’s another attack surface."
  - Rebuttal: "Our private option separates the control plane into a customer-managed VPC subnet (or on-prem pod); control plane APIs are authenticated via mutual TLS and integrate with your IdP and KMS. We provide audit logs and optional HSM integration so operators keep custody of keys."
  - Supporting detail: show network diagram (SE kit) that highlights control-plane endpoints inside customer VPC and optional VPN/DirectConnect. Point to infra runbook INFRA-782.

2) "If your control plane goes down we lose all inference traffic."
  - Rebuttal: "We design for graceful degradation: local inference runtime can continue serving pinned model variants and a last-known-config cache permits traffic until control plane recovers. For enterprise tiers we provide multi-region control-plane failover and documented SLA behaviors."
  - Supporting detail: cite failover timeline and local-config TTL (demo scripts show time-to-fallback ~30s for metadata).

3) "How do we prove there is no data leakage between tenants?"
  - Rebuttal: "Control plane metadata is strictly namespaced per tenant; data plane traffic never transits Redwood-managed networks unless you enable it. We give you SHA256-signed manifests and model checksums to validate runtime images."
  - Supporting detail: provide attestation artifact examples and KMS integration notes for auditors.

4) "We already have a self-hosted stack — why adopt Redwood Private?"
  - Rebuttal: "Redwood provides the orchestration, performance tuning, and rollout automation out-of-the-box (batching, KV cache, quantization profiles) and maintains the API contract so apps don’t need changes. Our differentiated value is ops reduction and unit-cost improvements compared with one-off stacks."
  - Supporting detail: include rough TCO comparison talking points (SE kit has sample numbers).

Competitive angles to raise proactively
- Versus fully managed cloud vendors: emphasize the control plane parity (we offer the same API surface and observability but with private control plane placement and customer-owned networking).
- Versus pure self-hosted inference vendors: emphasize our runtime optimizations and rollout tooling—customers pay less operational overhead and get consistent performance tuning maintained by Redwood.
- Versus open-source bundles + in-house orchestration: highlight accreditation and support — audited release process and enterprise support SLAs that reduce risk in regulated environments.

Recommended talk tracks by persona (short script snippets)
- To CISO: "We treat your network boundary as the primary enforcement point. Deployment options put control-plane endpoints into your VPC and use your keys. We produce continuous audit telemetry so you can verify change provenance during audits."
- To Platform Lead: "We plug into your CI/CD: image signing, ArgoCD/Terraform modules, and declarative manifests. You get canary rollouts, automated rollback policies, and cost/latency dashboards per model route."
- To Compliance: "We can document evidence for each stage of model lifecycle; we replay recent configuration changes and provide signed artifact manifests for auditors."

Technical appendix for SEs (one-paragraph summaries SEs can expand in deep dives)
- Control plane placement: options are (1) Redwood-managed tenant in a dedicated account with private endpoints, (2) control-plane components deployed into customer VPC (recommended for high-regulation buyers), or (3) fully on-prem control plane (air-gapped) with a lightweight synchronization agent.
- Authentication & keys: supports mutual TLS, SAML/OIDC for admin identity, and KMS/HSM for key custody. We do not store plaintext customer keys unless explicitly requested under a support contract.
- Failover & local caches: runtime maintains a signed config cache and KV cache to handle control-plane outages for a defined TTL.
- Observability: per-model and per-route telemetry exported to customer SIEM; token-level cost tracing available.

Proof points (pull these into customer slides)
- Pilot customer A (finserv): ran a private deployment in their VPC with KMS integration; no data plane egress and passed internal pen-test with minor findings remediated.
- Pilot customer B (healthcare): required deterministic audit trails; we delivered signed manifests and an attestation log used in their compliance report.
- Performance note: host-equivalent latency within 5–10% for pinned model configs vs Redwood hosted mode for similar instance types.

Demo & validation checklist for first SE call (aim for 45–60 min)
- Pre-call: send architecture sketch and slide with the three deployment options.
- On call (15m) product pitch and compliance framing.
- On call (20–30m) run a short demo connecting to a self-contained private control plane in a sandbox VPC: show API parity, perform a model rollout, and show audit log generation.
- Post-call: provide a checklist for their infra team (required firewall rules, KMS role, service account, and sample Terraform snippet).

Objections requiring legal/infra signoff (do not answer without confirmation)
- Requests to store customer-owned encryption keys inside Redwood-managed HSM in perpetuity (legal to confirm).
- Requests for contractual indemnities tied to on-prem third-party integrations (legal + sales ops review).

Open questions / action items
- Confirm telemetries we can expose to customer SIEMs without leaking PII (Action: Security to validate; target 2024-11-09).
- Finalize recommended default TTLs for signed control-plane cache (Action: Serving runtime to propose; target 2024-10-25).
- Create a minimal Terraform module template for SE sandbox demos (Action: Platform eng; PR referenced in linked artifacts).

Examples: short email opener for initial outreach
"Hi <Name>,
We ran a short on-prem pilot with a FinServ customer that needed KMS-in-customer-VPC and full auditability. We can show how Redwood keeps the runtime inside your boundary while providing the same API surface and rollout tooling your engineers expect. Would you be open to a 45-minute technical walkthrough next week?
— Sofia"

Appendix: quick reference artifacts for shareable SE kit
- Network diagram (one-pager) — concise view of control plane placement options (attached in SE kit).
- Table of supported integrations (KMS vendors, IdPs, SIEM endpoints).
- Small FAQ for auditors (signed manifests, evidence export, provenance).

Notes to reviewers:
- Please flag any phrasing that overpromises around HSM options — legal/security review required before public templates.
- If product wants different default phrasing for failover guarantees, propose alternate language inline.

End of brief.
